title: Low degree moment bound
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let $p$ be a coefficient family on subsets of the $n$ coordinates, and suppose $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>k$. For every real $t$ with $1<t<2$, writing $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\chi_S(x)$, one has $\displaystyle(t-1)^k\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2\leq\left(\mathbb E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)}|P(x)|^t\right)^{2/t}$.
hypotheses_covered: coefficient family $p$ on subsets of the $n$ coordinates
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients; degree at most $k$ means $a_S=0$ for $|S|>k$. If $P$ has degree at most the integer $k\ge0$ and $1<t<2$, then $(t-1)^k\sum_Sa_S^2\le(\mathbb E|P|^t)^{2/t}$.
